title: “Lord, help me remain faithful in the quiet work, trusting You even when the rain has not yet come.”
paragraphs: “Lord, help me remain faithful in the quiet work, trusting You even when the rain has not yet come.”

Witnessing Noah Build the Ark
📖 Genesis 6:22
When I read the Bible, it often feels like I am standing nearby, watching quietly.

I see him building—day after day—while the sky still looks calm.
I stay hidden, blending into the world around me, listening to the sound of wood meeting wood.
Obedience doesn’t hurry. It trusts.

⏸️ Pause here.
Would I keep building… if I were the only one who believed the rain was coming?
💭 What quiet act of faith might God be asking me to keep doing—without applause, without proof, only trust?
💭 Share what this moment stirs in you
What do you imagine it felt like to keep working while others doubted?
Where in your life are you called to obedience without immediate results?
How do you respond when faith feels lonely or misunderstood?
What helps you stay faithful when God’s promises feel distant?
